question: Which turn sense does a caDNAno 15 x 4 honeycomb x-raster carry, and does C-0119's 112 bp row survive it?

conditions.lattice: caDNAno honeycomb: three azimuths at 7 bp, 21 bp = 2 turns, scaffold crossovers 5 bp upstream or downstream of the staple lattice
conditions.naturalTwist: 10.5 base pairs per turn, which is the honeycomb's design twist
conditions.crossSection: design (i) of Douglas et al., 15 x-raster rows of 4 helices, 60 duplexes
conditions.handedness: B-DNA is right-handed; viewed from +z the backbone azimuth increases counter-clockwise with z, so one azimuth step (+7 bp) advances it by +240 = -120 degrees and neighbour class increases as azimuth falls
conditions.solve: NONE — the task is exact integer lattice arithmetic and no solve is justified on a lattice this repository's machinery does not model

quotations.corrugation: The x-raster rows within the honeycomb framework are corrugated; they stagger up and down and encompass helices that are actually at two different y-positions.
quotations.rasterOrder: as viewed down the helical axes, close-packing rows of helices were arrayed within the honeycomb framework in an x-raster pattern (i.e. left to right, then down, then right to left, then down, etc.)
quotations.allotment: Each helix was allotted 126 bases of scaffold. Of those 126 bases, 98 were paired with complementary staples, and the remaining 28 bases were divided into front and rear unpaired loop fragments at the ends of each helix.
quotations.scaffolds: The shapes were folded either from a 7560-base scaffold into 60 parallel helices or from an 8064-base scaffold into 64 parallel helices
quotations.loopsAreVisible: no obvious defects such as missing, broken, disrupted, or smeared out sections more than 3 nm away from the unpaired scaffold loops at the front and rear interfaces
quotations.source: Douglas, Marblestone, Teerapittayanon, Vazquez, Church and Shih, Nucleic Acids Research 37:5001 (2009), PMC2731887, read directly from gpd/data/T-151-sources/PMC2731887-fullTextXML.xml — zero fetches

predicates.statement: the cross-section geometry is READ, not assumed: the corrugation is a theorem of the honeycomb and the paper states it in one sentence
the turn sense is emitted per helix for every helix of design (i) with a defined one
the answer is invariant under the one free convention — mirroring the cross-section, or flipping which face the scaffold starts at — which swaps the two LABELS and not the alternation
the same machinery on the square sheet returns a CONSTANT sense, reproducing C-0086's unconditional rule
the consequence for 112 bp and for 119 bp is stated as a FRACTION of the helices
the cheapest departure from uniformity that restores admissibility is quoted, in base pairs and in nm

falsifiers.statement: consecutive helices of an x-raster row are on the SAME honeycomb sublattice
falsifiers.outcome: all 59 consecutive pairs of design (i) are A/B alternating, which is forced: no honeycomb path can continue in the same direction

falsifiers.statement: the GEOMETRIC sense is constant along the raster
falsifiers.outcome: it alternates in blocks of four — 1222211112222111 — one block per x-raster row plus the three helices each row turn contaminates

falsifiers.statement: the two alternations CANCEL, so the effective sense is constant and a uniform row length exists
falsifiers.outcome: they do NOT cancel: sense 1 on 28 helices and sense 2 on 30 of 58. They cancel WITHIN a row — every row interior carries one sense — and the m - 1 row turns break it, which is why a ONE-row raster is the only constant case

falsifiers.statement: the same machinery on the square sheet gives a non-constant sense, i.e. fails to reproduce C-0086
falsifiers.outcome: constant at 2, because 2 is its OWN NEGATIVE modulo 4 — which is exactly why C-0086's rule is unconditional and the honeycomb's cannot be

falsifiers.statement: the alternation verdict changes under the free viewing convention
falsifiers.outcome: mirroring swaps the two labels one for one and leaves both senses present

falsifiers.statement: the two honeycomb residue triples are not disjoint, contradicting C-0136
the paper's own per-helix allotment does not reproduce its two scaffold lengths
falsifiers.outcome: 60 x 126 = 7560 and 64 x 126 = 8064, both EXACT — so design (i), at 60 helices, is folded from p7560 and spends it to the last nucleotide

falsifiers.statement: some uniform row length serves BOTH turn senses
falsifiers.outcome: 0 of 2100 row lengths, which is a theorem: the two triples are disjoint mod 21

falsifiers.statement: the minimum admissible row-length stagger is not three base pairs
falsifiers.outcome: 3 bp = 1.0200 nm, from residue 7 against 4 and 17 against 14

findings: THE 15 x 4 X-RASTER CARRIES BOTH TURN SENSES, ALTERNATING, AND NEITHER 112 bp NOR 119 bp IS AVAILABLE AS A UNIFORM WIDTH. Sense 1 lands on 28 of its 58 helices with a defined sense and sense 2 on 30; the two admissible residue triples {7,17,18} and {3,4,14} are disjoint, so no single row length serves the tile. CH-0165's second branch is the one that obtains.

THE CHEAP BOUND IS A THEOREM AND IT RAN FIRST: a honeycomb path can never continue in the same direction, so an x-raster row is corrugated at every lattice — which is what the caDNAno paper states as "the x-raster rows … are corrugated; they stagger up and down". Consecutive helices of a row are therefore on opposite sublattices and the GEOMETRIC sense alternates.

THE TWO ALTERNATIONS CANCEL WITHIN A ROW AND THE ROW TURNS BREAK THEM. The scaffold runs the full length of every helix, so its axial direction alternates too, and Delta_eff = s . Delta_geom is CONSTANT along a row interior — consecutive rows carrying opposite senses. Each of the m - 1 row turns contaminates three helices. A ONE-row raster is the only case with a constant sense, and one corrugated row is two y-positions, not four layers.

THE SQUARE LATTICE'S UNCONDITIONALITY IS AN ACCIDENT OF 4 = 2 x 2. Its two in-plane neighbours are 180 degrees apart, i.e. two azimuth classes, and 2 is its own negative modulo 4 — so the axial-direction alternation cannot touch it and C-0086's rule needs no turn sense. Modulo 3 neither 1 nor 2 is self-inverse, which is the whole of the difference.

ROUTE A — AN ALL-CROSSOVER RASTER NEEDS TWO ROW LENGTHS, AND THE MINIMUM STAGGER IS 3 bp = 1.0200 nm. The best pair inside M13 at a stagger of at most 4 bp is 112 / 108 bp, an axial extent of 116 bp = 39.44 nm (-1.40 % of Sec 3's nominal 40.0 nm) on 6596 nucleotides, with the two faces ragged by 4 and 8 bp. That BEATS the square lattice's 38.08 nm at -4.80 % and C-0133's 37.40 nm at -6.50 %.

ROUTE B IS WHAT THE PAPER ACTUALLY BUILT, AND IT IS UNPAIRED LOOPS AT EVERY TURN. "Each helix was allotted 126 bases of scaffold. Of those 126 bases, 98 were paired with complementary staples, and the remaining 28 bases were divided into front and rear unpaired loop fragments at the ends of each helix." So every raster turn of the built blocks passes through 14 + 14 = 28 unpaired nucleotides, the residue condition does not bind them at all, and the TEM criterion names the loops as a visible feature.

THE LOOPS COST 1 680 NUCLEOTIDES ON A 60-HELIX TILE, AND M13 HAS 529 SPARE AT 112 bp. At the built allowance the widest four-layer honeycomb tile is 92 bp = 31.28 nm from M13 (-21.80 %) and 106 bp = 36.04 nm from p8064 (-9.90 %). C-0119's uniform 112 bp x 60 needs 8 400 nt with the loops and is out of reach of BOTH scaffolds.

DESIGN (i) IS FOLDED FROM p7560, NOT p8064, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS EXACT. 15 x 4 is 60 helices and 60 x 126 = 7 560 to the nucleotide; the 64-helix designs are (iii) 8 x 8 and (v) 4 x 16, and 64 x 126 = 8 064. C-0119 assigns p8064 to designs i, iii and v and therefore quotes a 1 344 nt remainder where the design's own scaffold leaves ZERO.

EVERY x-RASTER ROW THE PAPER FOLDED HAS AN EVEN NUMBER OF HELICES — 4, 6, 8, 10, 16, 20, 30 — and that is forced: a row's two ends must both carry the DOWNWARD vertical bond, and that bond points up on one sublattice and down on the other. An odd row cannot turn down at both ends.

C-0136'S OWN TABLE MIS-STATES ITS Delta = 1 NEAREST WIDTH. The nearest admissible Delta = 1 row length to 40.0 nm is 122 bp = 41.48 nm (+3.70 %), not the 112 bp = 38.08 nm its width table carries; C-0136's own result file has 122 in nearestDelta1WidthBasePairs. 112 bp is the nearest SQUARE-lattice width and an admissible Delta = 1 one, but it is not the nearest.
